acceptanceCriteria: A reproducible scale benchmark (synthetic stores of about 1k, 10k and 100k tickets with proportional receipts) measures every corvint-tasks read command (version, queue status, roadmap, ticket list/search/show with facets and --count, receipt audit) and the common writes (ticket create, claim, complete-manual), retaining wall time, allocations and open-descriptor peaks.
CPU and allocation profiles identify the dominant costs at each scale; each is either fixed or retained as a named limit with a ticket.
Read latency for count and search reads at 10k tickets is under 0.5 s warm on the development Mac, or the remaining gap is explained with evidence.
No change weakens receipt verification, authority, or read non-mutation (product invariant 4); stale or forged derived state falls back to full verification.
Per-command before/after timings at each scale are retained in a build-log entry.
body: Owner request 2026-10-09: corvint-tasks should be as optimized for performance as possible, including at large ticket counts. Related: V1-1051 (absent checkpoint forces full receipt audit on reads, 2-3 s on the real store of about 1,100 tickets), V1-0906 (O(receipts) file opens in WatchChanges and the complete-route audit), V1-0841 (completed descriptor exhaustion at 5000 receipts). There is no benchmark in internal/tasks today. Deliver a scale harness, profile, fix the dominant hot paths, and retain limits.
